whyThisShow: This one landed on the official 30 Trips Around the Sun box set, and the community had been talking about it long before that. One reviewer rated it his personal best out of everything he saw from 1978 through '95, saying "there was something in the air, something different, special, pretty damn unbelievable" [source: 'there was something in the air, something different, special, pretty damn unbelievable']. Another called it a top-five show across 150 Dead concerts seen [source: 'Definitely a top-5 among the 150 shows I saw from 1977-1995']. The setlist is not obviously special on paper — no Terrapin, no Estimated, no Shakedown — but one listener who flagged exactly that notes that "everything is played with such energy and soul that even the mediocre songs shine" [source: 'everything is played with such energy and soul that even the mediocre songs shine']. The Augusta Civic Center was a small room, and the people who were there keep coming back to that intimacy as the thing that made the night feel different.
listenFor: The Uncle John's Band is the centerpiece of the second set: at eleven minutes it drifts into a separate five-minute jam that one reviewer heard as sounding "like Dark Star, China Doll or Sage and Spirit all in one" [source: 'a 5 minute Jam that sounds like Dark Star, China Doll or Sage and Spirit all in one']. The Morning Dew follows directly and multiple attendees flag it as the emotional peak of the night — one listener described the scene as Brent's Leslie making the whole arena spin, with Phil's bombs hitting hard even through the mixed source [source: "Brent's Leslie is making the whole arena spin, and even on this AUD patch in Set Two, Phil's bombs are devastating"]. One taper noted the jamming "started towards the end of don't need love and carried right on thru Morning Dew" with no separate Space section breaking the flow [source: 'the jamming started towards the end of don't need love and carried right on thru Morning Dew']. The Playing in the Band reprise also draws attention: one reviewer called it "a fun little joke for those that were stoned enough to get it," a leftover from the previous night's show [source: 'a fun little joke for those that were stoned enough to get it'].
context: This is a soundboard recording from the fall 1984 east coast run, archived as gd84-10-12.sbd.clugston.5585.sbeok.shnf. The show was later officially released as part of the 30 Trips Around the Sun box set. Reviewers place it in the context of a strong October run that also included shows on 10/11 and 10/15, though one noted that the adjacent dates survive only as audience recordings [source: 'there was some serious competition from 10/11 and 10/15, both available only as AUD sources']. One reviewer described the 1984 soundboard sound as having "full, lots of bass, depth and a certain 1984 ambiance" [source: 'full, lots of bass, depth and a certain 1984 ambiance'].
funFact: One taper brought in thirty-eight pounds of digital audio processing equipment on his back and connected to Nakamichi mics on either side of the soundboard, losing count at around twenty-five DAT recorders running — and walked out with what he called "the un-interrupted master" [source: 'I lost count at about twenty five d-5 cassette recorders running from behind my d/a signal. On this night everything went right and I walked with the un-interrupted master'].
headline: Augusta, October '84 — the Dew left the lot silent.
